parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no trans-specific criminal offence: the 2013 Crimes Act repealed the impersonation provisions that targeted gender-diverse people, and gender presentation is no longer an offence. A long-standing third-gender tradition is embedded in chiefly land and title transmission, society is characterised as very tolerant of transgender identity, a 2026 Pride Week occurred, and the Sentencing Act aggravates crimes motivated by gender identity. The unenforced sodomy sections (no documented prosecutions) are a secondary, sexuality-law factor reaching a trans visitor only through relationship conduct. No border, document, facility or care exposure for visitors is documented either way, and no trans-specific violence record exists. Official resistance to decriminalisation and absent visitor-facing protections hold the score below the acceptance-with-protections tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry, visa, passport-marker or secondary-screening claim is documented in the inventory; document and screening exposure is unresolved rather than shown to be safe.
entry_documents.protection: No documented trans-specific border friction; the impersonation offence was repealed in 2013.
entry_documents.interaction: A document-appearance mismatch would interact with the still-live sodomy sections only through relationship conduct, which is documented as unenforced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Sections 67/68/71 remain in force with penalties up to 5-7 years and no defence of consent for section 67; the government rejected decriminalisation in 2010, 2011 and at UPR.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Overview states the law is not enforced; inventory records no prosecution under these sections. No trans-specific policing, extortion or arrest is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement rules for a detained trans visitor are not documented, so a sodomy charge's custody consequences remain an open question.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access, ward-placement or strip-search rule is documented for visitors in either direction.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No subnational variation exists: one statute book, one censorship board, so no patchwork of hostile districts.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absent local rules, any facility exposure would derive from unwritten institutional practice, which the record does not describe.

care_services.exposure: No emergency-care refusal, HRT import or ward-placement evidence for trans visitors is documented.
care_services.protection: Mental Health Act 2007 bars pathologising non-heterosexual orientation and bans conversion therapy by professionals; Sentencing Act aggravates gender-identity-motivated crime.
care_services.interaction: The Act addresses sexual orientation rather than gender identity, so its reach to a trans visitor's care is partial.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Head of government and UPR statements frame homosexuality as religiously and culturally impermissible, rejecting all but one decriminalisation recommendation; censorship board shows selective morality toward sexuality content.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Third-gender people described by government as integral members of society and heirs to chiefly titles; 2011 UN joint statement signed; impersonation law repealed after advocacy relief.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility is sexuality-framed, not gender-identity-framed, so a visibly trans visitor sits inside the tolerated third-gender category rather than the targeted one.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific, custody-related or family-visit rule is documented for a travelling parent or child.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented exposure specific to children travelling with a gender-diverse adult.
minors_guardians.interaction: Third-gender inheritance through extended family consensus suggests family inclusion, but its bearing on visiting minors is not sourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence figure, incident count or denominator exists; magnitude of street risk is unresolved in either direction.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented institutionalised third-gender tradition, chiefly titles, an active advocacy organisation and a 2026 Pride Week indicate social accommodation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The 'very tolerant' characterisation carries no survey, population or period, so it is suggestive rather than measured.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No standalone hate-crime charge exists (sentencing-stage only); no documented remedy mechanism specifically for a trans visitor refused service or questioned at a border.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Sentencing Act 2016 s.7(1)(h) and Labour Act s.20(2) evidences functional equality-motivated legal machinery in adjacent domains.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Whether enforcement practice and courts would act for a short-stay foreign trans complainant is unresolved; non-enforcement of sodomy sections rests on an uncited overview.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: Vellandra has a routine, universal entry bar engineered against transgender visitors with no remedy. This dossier documents no visitor-facing restriction at all — no register, no exclusion, no state-run outing mechanism. Official hostility here is sexuality-framed, not directed at gender presentation, which the 2013 repeal confirms.

Lower than this case: Kestrel Isles has documented, recurring secondary screening and discretionary refusal of entry applied to trans travellers. This dossier has no border exposure documented either way — an open question, which weighs far less than a known universal-exposure practice applied at every crossing.

Closest match: Meridia combines trained border treatment with an appeal tribunal and brief, non-criminalising friction. This jurisdiction matches the low-severity, no-criminalisation profile but lacks any documented border training or visitor remedy, and retains an unenforced but live sodomy statute with official resistance to repeal — a step below on both protection and climate.

Higher than this case: Vessalia has explicit equality law covering gender identity in public services, an independent oversight board, and documented compensation for a clinic refusal. This dossier has only sentencing-stage aggravation, no public-services protection for visitors, and unresolved document and care exposure, so it cannot reach the low-risk tier.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime presents no documented traveller-facing restriction: the impersonation offence targeting gender-diverse people was repealed in 2013, gender presentation is lawful, an institutionalised third-gender tradition carries chiefly titles, and society is characterised as very tolerant of transgender identity, culminating in a 2026 Pride Week. The live sodomy sections are unenforced with no recorded prosecutions, are sexuality- not gender-framed, and reach a trans visitor only through relationship conduct — a secondary factor that the rubric forbids from dominating. What holds the score out of the 0.80+ tier is absence rather than documented harm: no border, document, facility or care evidence exists for visitors, no visitor-specific remedy is shown, and the state officially resists decriminalisation, leaving non-enforcement an uncited claim rather than a guarantee.
